scope: J034 Build Systems à la Carte as a design vocabulary

claims.claim: Build-system design can separate task/dependency expressiveness, scheduling order, rebuilding policy, and persistent build information.
evidence: Build Systems à la Carte, DOI 10.1145/3236774
Build systems à la carte: Theory and practice, DOI 10.1017/S0956796820000088

claims.claim: Topological scheduling requires dependencies in advance; restarting and suspending schedulers support dynamic dependencies with distinct restart/suspension costs.

Dirty bits, verifying traces, constructive traces, and deep constructive traces encode progressively different reuse evidence and costs; deep constructive traces require determinism and lose early cutoff.
The pure task model does not automatically account for untracked dependencies, nondeterminism, or volatility; sandboxing may reduce but need not eliminate untracked state.
evidence: Build systems à la carte: Theory and practice, DOI 10.1017/S0956796820000088, section 8.3

claims.claim: Current Anneal evidence supports coarse explicit generation boundaries while several upstream systems retain their own internal freshness state; open document state is distinct from disk state.
Anneal acceptance/publication requires current identity, completeness, and freshness fences beyond ordinary build scheduling/rebuilding.
claims.role: design authority + bounded execution/model evidence + derived comparison

derived_judgment: Start with coarse explicit DAG orchestration and explicit generation/result authority. Add dynamic dependency tracking, constructive caching, or finer-grained query infrastructure only when the corresponding dependency visibility, identity/determinism assumptions, and measured workload justify them. This is derived analysis, not adopted Anneal policy.
